mainTopic: תשובה arguments between Israel and the נביאים, and בלעם, the first of the four commoners who lose עולם הבא
overview: This amud opens by finishing a reading of a פסוק in תהלים as hints to דוד's enemies, and הקדוש ברוך הוא promises to make דוד and them friends. Next, רב and שמואל each explain the 'winning answer' Israel gave the נביא when told to do תשובה. הקדוש ברוך הוא replies that He never divorced or sold Israel, and ריש לקיש adds that נבוכדנצר is called 'My servant' so that Israel still belongs to God. רב נחמן welcomes God's anger in a פסוק from יחזקאל if it brings redemption, and רבה בר בר חנה shows Israel blaming the יצר הרע. The גמרא then returns to the משנה's four commoners and explains the names of בלעם and his father, who is also called כושן רשעתים and לבן. From the משנה it infers that other gentiles can reach עולם הבא, following רבי יהושע against רבי אליעזר. It ends with stories about בלעם: the alliance of מואב and מדין, the power of חוצפה, his physical defects, and a dispute about his immoral behavior that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Moab and Edom: גחזי and דואג
steps.stepSummary: Finishing the line about אחיתופל, the גמרא reads 'Moab is My washing pot' as גחזי and 'Over Edom I will cast My shoe' as דואג האדומי.
steps.simpleTranslation: [אחיתופל], who comes from יהודה. 'Moab is My washing pot': this is גחזי, who was punished over a matter of washing. 'Over Edom I will cast My shoe': this is דואג האדומי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading each phrase of the פסוק as a hint to one of the famous sinners. Here it matches 'Moab' to גחזי and 'Edom' to דואג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening words finish an earlier line that explained 'יהודה מחקקי' as אחיתופל, who came from שבט יהודה. 'Washing pot' points to גחזי because his sin and punishment were tied to washing. 'Edom' points to דואג because the פסוקים call him האדומי.

keyTerms.meaning: אלישע's servant, who was punished with צרעת
Doeg the Edomite, שאול's official and an enemy of דוד

phrases.english: who comes from Judah.
"Moab is My washing pot"
this is Gehazi,
who was struck over matters of washing.
phrases.notes: This is about גחזי. נעמן was told to wash in the ירדן, and גחזי took money from him and was struck with צרעת (מלכים ב 5).

phrases.english: "Over Edom I will cast My shoe"
this is Doeg the Edomite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the reading of the פסוק from the previous daf, phrase by phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Moab = גחזי (washing); Edom = דואג האדומי.

steps.title: The angels ask about דוד, and God promises to make them friends
steps.stepSummary: 'Philistia, cry aloud' is read as the angels asking what God will do if דוד objects, and God answers that He will make דוד and his enemies friends.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Philistia, cry aloud because of Me': the מלאכי השרת said before הקדוש ברוך הוא: Master of the world, if דוד, who killed the Philistine and gave Your children גת, comes, what will You do for him? He said to them: It is on Me to make them friends with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The last phrase of the פסוק becomes a short conversation between the angels and הקדוש ברוך הוא about how to handle דוד and his enemies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הִתְרוֹעָעִי' is read like 'רֵיעִים', friends. The angels worry that דוד, a great hero, would object to how his enemies are treated. God's answer is that He Himself will bring them to friendship, so דוד will not be hurt.

keyTerms.meaning: cry aloud. Here it is read as 'make friends'
gave as an inheritance, gave possession of

phrases.english: "Philistia, cry aloud because of Me"
phrases.notes: The word הִתְרוֹעָעִי sounds like רֵיעִים, friends. That is the hook for what follows.

phrases.english: the ministering angels said
before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the Universe,
if David comes
who killed the Philistine
and gave Your children Gath as an inheritance,
what will You do for him?
He said to them:
It is upon Me to make them friends with each other.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָלַי פְּלֶשֶׁת הִתְרוֹעָעִי אָמְרוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the same פסוק with its last phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God will Himself make דוד and his enemies friends.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole פסוק in תהלים is read as hints to דוד's enemies. Its ending shows that God will make peace between דוד and them.

steps.title: רב: Israel's 'winning answer' is that the prophets died too
steps.stepSummary: רב explains 'מְשֻׁבָה נִצַּחַת' as a winning reply. When the נביא said 'Your sinning fathers are dead,' Israel answered, 'So are your prophets who did not sin!'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Why has this people of Jerusalem turned away with a lasting backsliding?' רב said: כנסת ישראל gave the נביא a winning answer. The נביא said to Israel: Do תשובה! Your fathers who sinned, where are they? They said to him: And your prophets who did not sin, where are they? As it says: 'Your fathers, where are they? And the prophets, do they live forever?'
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב reads a פסוק in ירמיהו as describing a sharp comeback Israel gave the נביא when he told them to do תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads 'נִצַּחַת' as 'winning' instead of 'lasting.' The נביא's argument was: sinners die, so repent. Israel's comeback was: righteous prophets die too, so death proves nothing about sin.

keyTerms.meaning: lasting backsliding. רב reads it as 'a winning reply'
the community of Israel as a whole

phrases.english: "Why has this people turned away,
Jerusalem, with a lasting backsliding, etc."
Rav said:
a winning answer
phrases.notes: Here תְּשׁוּבָה means a reply, not repentance. רב reads נִצַּחַת as coming from 'to win.'

phrases.english: the congregation of Israel answered the prophet.
The prophet said to Israel:
Repent!
Your fathers who sinned, where are they?
They said to him:
And your prophets who did not sin, where are they?
as it says:
"Your fathers, where are they?
And the prophets, do they live forever?"

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב תְּשׁוּבָה נִצַּחַת הֵשִׁיבָה כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לַנָּבִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: a new פסוק and a new explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'winning answer' was: the righteous prophets also died, so death is no proof of sin.
steps.confusionAlert: In this step תְּשׁוּבָה means 'an answer,' not 'repentance.' The wordplay depends on both meanings of the same word.

steps.title: The prophet replies: your fathers admitted their sins
steps.stepSummary: The נביא answers that the fathers themselves came back and admitted that the prophets' warnings came true.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Your fathers came back and admitted it, as it says: 'But My words and My statutes, which I commanded My servants the prophets, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The נביא pushes back on Israel's comeback with the next פסוק in זכריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is not who died, but what the fathers admitted before they died. The rest of the פסוק says the fathers did תשובה and admitted that God punished them for their ways. So the warnings were proven true.

phrases.english: He said to them:
(Your fathers) went back and admitted,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, but either way it is the fathers who admitted.

phrases.english: as it says:
"But My words and My statutes

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר צִוִּיתִי אֶת עֲבָדַי הַנְּבִיאִים וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: which I commanded My servants the prophets, etc."
phrases.notes: זכריה 1:6. The rest of the פסוק says the fathers did תשובה and admitted God judged them rightly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replies to Israel's comeback in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shifts the proof from death to the fathers' own confession.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Israel argued that since prophets also die, death proves nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fathers admitted the warnings came true, which proves that sin brings punishment.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, Israel's clever answer was about death, and the נביא answered with the fathers' own admission.

steps.title: שמואל: the claim of a sold slave and a divorced wife
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the winning answer was different. Ten men told the נביא that a sold slave and a divorced wife no longer belong to their old master or husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Ten people came and sat before him. He said to them: Do תשובה! They said to him: A slave whose master sold him, and a woman whose husband divorced her, does this one have any claim on that one at all?
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a second explanation of the 'winning answer.' This time it is an argument that the bond between God and Israel was cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The men compare themselves to a sold slave and a divorced wife. Since God handed them over to other nations, they argue, He has no claim on them anymore. So, they say, He cannot demand תשובה.

keyTerms.meaning: a slave whose master sold him
a woman whose husband divorced her

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
Ten people came
and sat before him.
He said to them: Repent!
They said to him:
A slave whose master sold him,
and a woman whose husband divorced her,

phrases.aramaic: כְּלוּם יֵשׁ לָזֶה עַל זֶה כְּלוּם?
phrases.english: does this one have any claim on that one at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר בָּאוּ עֲשָׂרָה בְּנֵי אָדָם וְיָשְׁבוּ לְפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another way of explaining the 'winning answer' from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The winning answer was: God gave us away like a sold slave or a divorced wife, so the bond is broken.

steps.title: God answers: no divorce, no sale
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא sends the נביא to answer with ישעיהו 50:1. There was never a divorce document or a sale; Israel was only sent away because of its sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to the נביא: Go say to them: 'Where is your mother's bill of divorce with which I sent her away? Or which of My creditors did I sell you to? Behold, for your sins you were sold, and for your crimes your mother was sent away.'
steps.whatsHappening: God answers the slave and wife argument directly with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real divorce needs a document, and a real sale needs a buyer. God says neither exists. Israel was sent away as a punishment, not cut off, so the bond still stands and תשובה is still expected.

keyTerms.meaning: My creditors, people I owe money to

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַנָּבִיא:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to the prophet:
Go say to them:
"Where is your mother's bill of divorce
with which I sent her away?
Or which of My creditors
is it to whom I sold you?
Behold, for your sins you were sold,
and for your crimes your mother was sent away."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַנָּבִיא לֵךְ אֱמוֹר לָהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the argument made in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denies that a sale or divorce ever happened.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Israel thought it had been sold or divorced, so the bond was over.
steps.terutzMaskana: There was no divorce document and no sale. Israel was only sent away for its sins and still belongs to God.

steps.title: ריש לקיש asks: why is נבוכדנצר called 'My servant'?
steps.stepSummary: To support שמואל, the גמרא brings ריש לקיש's question: how can the same title, 'My servant,' be used for both דוד and נבוכדנצר?
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what ריש לקיש said: What is the meaning of what is written, 'דוד My servant' and 'נבוכדנצר My servant'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects שמואל's story to a teaching of ריש לקיש. It starts with his question, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is surprising that the wicked נבוכדנצר gets the same title as the righteous דוד. The answer will show that this title protects God's ownership of Israel.

keyTerms.meaning: and this is what [so-and-so] said, a phrase that brings a supporting teaching

phrases.english: And this is what Reish Lakish said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"David My servant,"
"Nebuchadnezzar My servant"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a supporting teaching for שמואל's story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is נבוכדנצר given the same title, 'My servant,' as דוד?

steps.title: A servant's property belongs to his master
steps.stepSummary: God knew Israel would claim it had been sold, so He called נבוכדנצר His servant in advance. Whatever a servant acquires belongs to the master.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is revealed and known before the One Who spoke and the world came to be that Israel would one day say this. Therefore הקדוש ברוך הוא acted ahead of time and called him His servant. A slave who acquired property: the slave belongs to whom? The property belongs to whom?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers his own question. Calling נבוכדנצר 'My servant' means that even after Israel is handed to him, it still belongs to God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that whatever a slave acquires belongs to his master. If נבוכדנצר is God's slave, then Israel, which he 'acquired,' is still God's. So the 'we were sold' argument from step 5 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: the One Who spoke and the world came to be, a name for God

phrases.english: It is revealed and known before
the One Who spoke and the world came to be
that Israel would one day say this,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the claim from שמואל's story: 'we were sold, so we're no longer His.'

phrases.english: therefore the Holy One, Blessed be He, acted ahead of time
and called him His servant.
A slave who acquired property:
the slave belongs to whom? The property belongs to whom?

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ לִפְנֵי מִי שֶׁאָמַר וְהָיָה הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's question from step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נבוכדנצר is called God's servant so that Israel, handed to him, still belongs to God, the way a slave's property belongs to his master.
steps.whatToRemember: Israel was never really cut off from God. No divorce, no sale, and even the conqueror is God's servant, so whatever he 'owns' is God's.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the argument that exile ended the bond with God. Israel still belongs to Him, so the call to do תשובה still applies.

steps.title: God swears He will rule over Israel and not let them go
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק from יחזקאל shows that Israel's plan to become like the nations will never happen, because God will rule over them by force.
steps.simpleTranslation: "What you are thinking will never happen, when you say: We will be like the nations and serve wood and stone. As I live, says God, with a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and poured-out anger, I will rule over you."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק from יחזקאל in which Israel wants to be like the nations, and God swears this will never happen. This sets up רב נחמן's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Israel says it will become like the other nations and serve idols. God answers with an oath that He will rule over them, even with a strong hand and poured-out anger. The theme fits the earlier steps about Israel not being cut off, but the גמרא quotes this פסוק mainly for רב נחמן's comment that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: what comes into your mind, what you are planning
to serve wood and stone, meaning idols

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the bond between God and Israel cannot be cancelled, not even by Israel's own wish to leave.

phrases.english: "And what comes into your mind shall never come to be,
that you say: We will be like the nations,
like the families of the lands, serving wood and stone.
As I live, says the Lord God,

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא בְּיָד חֲזָקָה וּבִזְרוֹעַ נְטוּיָה
phrases.english: surely with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm
phrases.notes: "אם לא" here is the language of an oath, so it means "surely," not "if not."

phrases.english: and with wrath poured out, will I rule over you."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָעֹלָה עַל רוּחֲכֶם הָיוֹ לֹא תִהְיֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes a new פסוק on the same theme as step 8 (Israel is not free to leave God), as the base text for רב נחמן's comment in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: Israel's claim that it is free from God, like a sold slave or a divorced wife

steps.title: רב נחמן: let God be angry at us, as long as He redeems us
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן reads the פסוק as good news: he would accept all that anger if it ends in redemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Let God be angry at us with all that anger, and redeem us.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן comments on the פסוק just quoted, and he hears it as a promise rather than only a threat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says God will rule over Israel 'with poured-out anger.' רב נחמן focuses on the words 'I will rule over you.' Being ruled by God, even with anger, means God is still keeping Israel as His own, and that is worth any price if it leads to redemption.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
With all of this kind of wrath,
let the Merciful One be angry at us,
and redeem us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A comment on the פסוק from יחזקאל quoted in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God's anger is welcome if it comes along with redemption, because it shows He is still ruling over Israel.

steps.title: Israel blames the יצר הרע and says God must fix it
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה explains a פסוק in ישעיהו as a conversation: the נביא tells Israel to repent, and Israel says the יצר הרע is too strong, so God should handle it.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the פסוק "And chastise in judgment; his God will instruct him," רבה בר בר חנה said: The נביא told Israel, 'Repent!' They said, 'We can't. The יצר הרע controls us.' He said, 'Then discipline your יצר!' They said, 'His God will instruct him.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another short story of the נביא arguing with Israel. Each time the נביא tells them what to do, they push the job back onto God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words of the פסוק are read as two speakers. The first part, 'and chastise,' is the נביא telling them to discipline their יצר. The second part, 'his God will instruct him,' is Israel's reply: God should control the יצר, because we cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: will instruct him, will guide him

steps.whatToRemember: This ends the part about the arguments between the נביאים and Israel: Israel kept finding reasons why it was not their fault.

phrases.english: "And chastise in judgment; his God will instruct him":
Rabba bar bar Ḥana said:
The prophet said to the Jewish people:
Repent!
They said to him: We cannot,
the evil inclination rules over us.
He said to them: Discipline your inclinations!
They said to him: "His God will instruct him."
phrases.notes: They mean God should teach the יצר to let us win, because we cannot beat it alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: One more example of Israel answering back to the נביא, like the exchanges in steps 3 and 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק is read as a dialogue in which Israel blames the יצר הרע and puts the job of controlling it on God.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: the four commoners
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's list of four הדיוטות: בלעם, דואג, אחיתופל, and גחזי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Four commoners: בלעם, דואג, אחיתופל, and גחזי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes its list of four people. This is a setup line: the next steps will explain these names one by one, starting with בלעם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא was discussing kings and the arguments of the נביאים. Now it begins a new section on the four ordinary people the משנה lists as losing עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: commoners, people who were not kings
the gentile prophet hired to curse Israel

phrases.english: Four commoners:
Balaam, Doeg, Ahithophel, and Gehazi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadah about the נביאים and Israel and returns to the next part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה lists four commoners who lose עולם הבא.

steps.title: What the names בלעם and בן בעור hint at
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads בלעם's name as 'without a people' or 'wore out the people,' and reads 'son of בעור' as a hint that he sinned with an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: בלעם means 'without a people.' Another explanation: בלעם means 'he wore out the people.' 'Son of בעור' means he had relations with an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains בלעם's name by breaking it into Hebrew words that describe his wickedness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reading, בלא עם, fits the משנה: he has no share with the Jewish people in עולם הבא. The second reading, בלה עם, describes what he did, wearing down Israel. The name of his father, בעור, is linked to בעיר, an animal.

phrases.english: Balaam: without a nation.
Alternatively: Balaam, who wore down the people.
Son of Beor: who had relations with an animal.
phrases.notes: בעיר means an animal; the name בעור sounds like it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first name in the משנה's list from step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The names בלעם and בן בעור point to his wickedness and his loss of a share with the Jewish people.

steps.title: A ברייתא: בעור, כושן רשעתים, and לבן are one person
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that בלעם's father בעור is the same man as כושן רשעתים and לבן הארמי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: He is בעור, he is כושן רשעתים, he is לבן הארמי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that connects בלעם's father to two other villains in תנ"ך. The next steps explain each name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three names from different places in תנ"ך are said to belong to one person. This makes בלעם's father a long-time enemy of Israel.

keyTerms.meaning: a king who oppressed Israel in the days of the שופטים

phrases.english: It was taught: He is Beor,
he is Cushan-Rishathaim,
he is Laban the Aramean.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the mention of בן בעור in step 13 by telling us more about בעור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בעור, כושן רשעתים, and לבן הארמי are the same person.

steps.title: Why he was called בעור and כושן רשעתים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains the names: בעור because he sinned with an animal, and כושן רשעתים because he did two evils to Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: בעור, because he had relations with an animal. כושן רשעתים, because he did two evil acts to Israel: one in the days of יעקב and one in the days of the שופטים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains why this one man had each of these names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רשעתים is read as 'two evils.' The first evil was against יעקב, which fits לבן, and the second was in the time of the שופטים, which fits כושן רשעתים. This is how one man can be both people.

keyTerms.meaning: the time when the judges judged

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא repeats the explanation of בעור from step 13. It is not a mistake; the ברייתא is giving its own reason for each of the three names.

phrases.english: Beor: because he had relations with an animal.

phrases.aramaic: כּוּשַׁן רִשְׁעָתַיִם – דַּעֲבַד שְׁתֵּי רִשְׁעָיוֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל:
phrases.english: Cushan-Rishathaim: because he did two evil acts to the Jewish people:
one in the days of Jacob,
and one in the days when the judges judged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the names listed in the ברייתא in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each name describes a different wicked act of the same man.

steps.title: So what was his real name?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks which of the three names was his actual name.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what was his name?
steps.whatsHappening: Since he has three names, the ברייתא asks which one was his real name. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two of the names, בעור and כושן רשעתים, were just explained as nicknames based on his sins. So the question is: what was he actually called?

phrases.english: And what was his actual name?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 15: two of the names were explained as nicknames.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the three names was his true name

steps.title: His real name was לבן הארמי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that his real name was לבן הארמי.
steps.simpleTranslation: His name was לבן הארמי.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question: his true name was לבן הארמי, and the other two were nicknames.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בעור and כושן רשעתים describe his sins, while לבן was his actual given name. So בלעם, the first of the four הדיוטות, was the son of לבן, who had been an enemy of Israel since יעקב's time.
steps.whatToRemember: בלעם's father had three names: בעור, כושן רשעתים, and his real name, לבן הארמי.

phrases.english: His name was Laban the Aramean.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His actual name was לבן הארמי; בעור and כושן רשעתים were descriptive nicknames.

steps.title: Two different wordings for בלעם's father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that one פסוק calls בלעם 'son of בעור' and another seems to say 'his son בעור.'
steps.simpleTranslation: One פסוק says 'בן בעור' (son of בעור), and another says 'בנו בעור' (his son, בעור).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices two different wordings about בלעם and his father and sets up a puzzle. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בן בעור' plainly means בלעם is the son of בעור. 'בנו בעור' can be read as 'his son is בעור,' which sounds as though בעור is בלעם's son. The two פסוקים seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: His son, בעור (can be read 'his son is בעור')

phrases.english: It is written: "Son of בעור,"
and it is written: "His son, בעור."
phrases.notes: במדבר 24:3. Read it as 'his son is בעור,' and you can see the problem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of בלעם's father's names by raising a wording puzzle about him.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain reading of בלעם's relationship to בעור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two פסוקים seem to reverse who is the father and who is the son.

steps.title: His father was like his son in prophecy
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that בעור was like a 'son' to בלעם when it came to נבואה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: His father was like a son to him in prophecy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן resolves the puzzle. Both פסוקים are true, each in a different sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In real life בעור is the father. But in נבואה, בלעם was far greater, so בעור ranked below him like a son. That is why the פסוק can call בעור 'his son.'

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן says:
His father was his son in prophecy.
phrases.notes: He means בלעם was the much greater נביא, so his father ranked below him like a student or son.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אָבִיו בְּנוֹ הוּא לוֹ בִּנְבִיאוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording contradiction raised in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each פסוק describes a different kind of relationship: physical versus prophetic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים seem to contradict each other about who is father and who is son.
steps.terutzMaskana: בעור is the physical father, but in prophecy he was below בלעם, like a son.

steps.title: Inference from the משנה: other gentiles can reach עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: Because the משנה names only בלעם, the גמרא infers that other gentiles do come to עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is בלעם who does not come to עולם הבא. That implies other gentiles do come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and reads an implied message from it. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה singled out בלעם as a gentile with no share in עולם הבא. If every gentile lacked a share, there would be no reason to name him. So the משנה implies that other gentiles can have a share.

keyTerms.meaning: But (implies that), used to draw an inference

phrases.aramaic: בִּלְעָם הוּא דְּלָא אָתֵי לְעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי,
phrases.english: It is בלעם who does not come to the World to Come,
but others do come.
phrases.notes: 'Others' here means other gentiles, not בלעם.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּלְעָם הוּא דְּלָא אָתֵי לְעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי, הָא אַחֲרִינֵי אָתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side point about names and returns to the wording of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה implies that gentiles other than בלעם can have a share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: Whose view is the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that gentiles can reach עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא the משנה follows. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the inference is clear, the גמרא wants to match it to a known opinion. This hints that not everyone agrees that gentiles can have a share.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is the משנה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the inference made in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that gentiles other than בלעם can have a share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: It follows רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי יהושע and introduces a ברייתא to show it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the view of רבי יהושע, as a ברייתא teaches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the משנה follows רבי יהושע. It is about to quote a ברייתא that shows his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer names the תנא first. The proof is the ברייתא that follows, where רבי יהושע argues with רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: It is רבי יהושע, as it is taught:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יהושע, as shown in the ברייתא that comes next.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the פסוק includes all gentiles
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר reads the פסוק as two groups going to שאול: Jewish sinners and all the gentiles.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: 'The wicked shall return to שאול, all the nations that forget God.' 'The wicked' are Jewish sinners; 'all the nations' are the gentile sinners.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא first gives רבי אליעזר's reading of a פסוק in תהלים. This is the view רבי יהושע will argue against.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר splits the פסוק into two halves. The first half covers sinful Jews. The second half, 'all the nations,' covers the gentiles, and the word 'all' sounds as though every gentile goes to שאול.

keyTerms.meaning: To שאול, the place of punishment

phrases.english: רבי אליעזר says,
"The wicked shall return to שאול,
all the nations that forget God."
"The wicked shall return to שאול":
these are the sinners of Israel,
"All the nations that forget God":
these are the sinners of the gentiles,
these are the words of רבי אליעזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, ״יָשׁוּבוּ רְשָׁעִים לִשְׁאוֹלָה כׇּל גּוֹיִם שְׁכֵחֵי אֱלֹהִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the ברייתא quoted to support the answer in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, the פסוק sends Jewish sinners and the gentiles to שאול, so the gentiles have no share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: the פסוק does not say 'like all the nations'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע objects that the פסוק only speaks of the nations 'that forget God,' not all nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: Does it say 'like all the nations'? It only says 'all the nations that forget God'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע attacks רבי אליעזר's reading by looking closely at the words of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To mean every gentile, the פסוק would need to say something like 'בכל גוים.' Instead it adds a limit: only the nations 'that forget God.' So gentiles who do not forget God are not included.

phrases.english: רבי יהושע said to him:
But does it say "like all the nations"?
Surely it says only
"all the nations that forget God"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: וְכִי נֶאֱמַר ״בְּכׇל גּוֹיִם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אליעזר's reading from step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's claim that the פסוק covers all gentiles
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words 'that forget God' limit the group, so the פסוק cannot mean every gentile.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's reading: the wicked are those who forget God
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע reads the whole פסוק as one group: the wicked who go to שאול are the nations that forget God.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, 'the wicked shall return to שאול.' Who are they? 'All the nations that forget God.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע gives his own reading of the פסוק. This shows why the משנה matches his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהושע, the second half of the פסוק explains the first half: the 'wicked' are the gentiles who forget God. So gentiles who do not forget God do have a share in עולם הבא, just as the משנה implied.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה follows רבי יהושע: only gentiles who 'forget God' lose עולם הבא, so righteous gentiles can have a share. בלעם is named because he was not one of them.
steps.confusionAlert: Both תנאים quote the same פסוק. They argue only about whether the second half adds a new group (רבי אליעזר) or explains who the first group is (רבי יהושע).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known idea that righteous gentiles have a share in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: Rather, "The wicked shall return to שאול":
Who are they?
"All the nations that forget God."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יהושע's argument from step 24 with his own reading.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only gentiles who forget God go to שאול. Other gentiles can reach עולם הבא, which fits the משנה's singling out of בלעם.

steps.title: בלעם gave a sign about his own fate
steps.stepSummary: בלעם himself said that how he died would show whether he had a share in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: That wicked man also gave a sign about himself. He said: 'Let me die the death of the upright.' If I die the death of the upright, 'my end will be like his.' If not, 'I am going to my people.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that בלעם's own words point to his fate. His words connect to the משנה's statement that he has no share in עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא joins two of בלעם's statements into one condition. If he dies like the upright, his end will be like Israel's and he gets a share. If not, he goes to 'his people,' the wicked who have no share.
steps.whatToRemember: בלעם tied his own fate to the way he would die: like the upright means a share, otherwise he joins his wicked people.

phrases.english: And that wicked man also
gave a sign about himself.
He said: "Let my soul die the death of the upright."
If my soul dies the death of the upright,
"let my end be like his,"
and if not,
"here I am going to my people."
phrases.notes: במדבר 24:14. 'My people' means the wicked of his nation, who have no share.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע נָתַן סִימָן בְּעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to בלעם, the subject of the משנה, after settling whose view the משנה follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בלעם's own words make his share in עולם הבא depend on dying the death of the upright. Otherwise he goes with his wicked people.

steps.title: Old enemies join together, like two dogs against a wolf
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that מואב and מדין were always enemies, but they united against ישראל, like two hostile dogs who team up to kill a wolf.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says the elders of מואב and the elders of מדין went together. A ברייתא teaches that these two nations never had peace. It is like two dogs guarding a flock who hated each other. A wolf attacked one of them. The other dog thought: if I don't help him, the wolf kills him today and comes for me tomorrow. So both dogs went and killed the wolf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק showing מואב and מדין acting together, and a ברייתא explains with a parable why two enemies would cooperate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is bothered that these two nations, who were always fighting, suddenly appear side by side. The parable answers that a shared danger, here ישראל, makes enemies into partners. Each one is really protecting himself.

phrases.english: "And the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian went."
It was taught: Midian and Moab
never had peace between them.
A parable: two dogs that were with the flock,
and they were hostile to one another.
A wolf came and attacked one of them.
The other one said: If I don't help him,

phrases.aramaic: הַיּוֹם הוֹרֵג אוֹתוֹ, וּלְמָחָר בָּא עָלַי.
phrases.english: today it kills him, and tomorrow it comes after me.
They both went and killed the wolf.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: מִדְיָן וּמוֹאָב לֹא הָיָה לָהֶם שָׁלוֹם מֵעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from בלעם's share in עולם הבא to a new set of פסוקים about the elders who came to hire him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מואב and מדין, lifelong enemies, united only because they both felt threatened by ישראל.

steps.title: A folk saying: the weasel and the cat feast together
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא connects the ברייתא to a popular saying about two enemies feasting at a third party's expense.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is what people say: a weasel and a cat made a wedding feast from the fat of the unlucky one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a well-known saying that matches the lesson of the dogs and the wolf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A weasel and a cat normally fight, but they happily share a meal when someone else is the victim. The same was true of מואב and מדין, who united only to hurt ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say (introduces a folk saying)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
This is what people say:
A weasel and a cat
made a wedding feast
from the fat of the unlucky one.
phrases.notes: בִּישׁ גַּדָּא literally means "bad luck". It refers to the poor third party who ends up being the meal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the ברייתא's lesson with a popular proverb.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Enemies will cooperate when someone else pays the price.

steps.title: Where did the princes of מדין go?
steps.stepSummary: The next פסוק mentions only the princes of מואב staying with בלעם, so the גמרא asks what happened to the princes of מדין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "And the princes of מואב stayed with בלעם." So where did the princes of מדין go?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that מדין suddenly disappears from the פסוק and asks where they went.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק earlier, both מואב and מדין came together. Now only מואב is said to stay overnight, so the גמרא wants to know why מדין dropped out.

phrases.english: "And the princes of Moab stayed with Balaam."
And the princes of Midian, where did they go?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the story to the next פסוק and notices a missing group.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why only the princes of מואב, and not those of מדין, stayed with בלעם.

steps.title: מדין left: no father hates his son
steps.stepSummary: When בלעם said he would ask ה׳ first, the princes of מדין gave up and left, sure that ה׳ would never let ישראל be cursed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once בלעם told them, "Stay here tonight and I will bring you an answer," they said: Is there any father who hates his son?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the princes of מדין left as soon as they heard that בלעם would ask ה׳ for permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They reasoned that ה׳ is like a father to ישראל, and a father will not agree to curse his own son. So they saw no point in waiting and went home.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there at all...? (a rhetorical question)

phrases.english: Once he said to them:
"Lodge here tonight,
and I will bring you back an answer,"
they said: Is there any father
who hates his son?
phrases.notes: They mean: if בלעם is going to ask ה׳‎, ה׳ will surely protect His children, ישראל. So they left.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דַּאֲמַר לְהוּ: ״לִינוּ פֹה הַלַּיְלָה וַהֲשִׁיבֹתִי אֶתְכֶם דָּבָר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of where the princes of מדין went.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They left once בלעם said he would ask ה׳, because they were sure ה׳ would not allow His children to be cursed.

steps.title: חוצפה works even toward Heaven
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן learns from בלעם that pushing boldly can get results even from ה׳: first ה׳ said "Don't go," and later "Go."
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: חוצפה works even toward Heaven. At first it is written, "Do not go with them," and in the end it is written, "Get up, go with them."
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן teaches a lesson about חוצפה and proves it from how ה׳'s answer to בלעם changed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בלעם was told clearly not to go, but he kept asking anyway. In the end ה׳ let him go. רב נחמן sees this as proof that bold persistence can have an effect even before ה׳.
steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is describing what happened with בלעם, not praising חוצפה. He is saying it can work, not that it is a good trait.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Impudence works even toward Heaven.
At first it is written: "You shall not go with them,"
and in the end it is written: "Get up, go with them."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the בלעם story and draws a general lesson from ה׳'s changing answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bold persistence can bring results even before ה׳, as seen with בלעם.

steps.title: חוצפה is kingship without a crown
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת adds that חוצפה gives a person almost the power of a king, proving it from דוד's words about the sons of צרויה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: חוצפה is kingship without a crown, as it is written: "And I am weak today, though anointed king, and these men, the sons of צרויה, are harder than me."
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives a second teaching about חוצפה and brings a פסוק from דוד המלך to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד was the anointed king, yet he admitted that the bold sons of צרויה were stronger than he was. Their nerve gave them power like a king's, missing only the crown.

keyTerms.meaning: The sons of צרויה (יואב and his brothers)

steps.whatToRemember: Two views on חוצפה: רב נחמן says it works even toward Heaven, and רב ששת says it gives power close to that of a king.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
Impudence is kingship without a crown,
as it is written: "And I am weak today,
though anointed king;
and these men, the sons of Zeruiah,
are too hard for me, etc."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 3:39. This is דוד speaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second אמורא's teaching on the same theme of חוצפה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוצפה gives a person power almost equal to a king's, lacking only the crown.

steps.title: בלעם limped on one leg and was blind in one eye
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads פסוקים to show that בלעם was lame in one leg and blind in one eye, while שמשון was lame in both legs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: בלעם was lame in one leg, as it says, "He went limping." שמשון was lame in both legs, as it says, "an adder on the path that bites the horse's heels." בלעם was blind in one eye, as it says, "whose eye is open."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן reads the wording of three פסוקים to teach physical details about בלעם and שמשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שפי means limping, so בלעם limped on one leg. שמשון's פסוק uses שפיפון, which sounds like שפי doubled, so he limped on both legs. The פסוק about בלעם says "the eye" in the singular, showing only one eye was working.

keyTerms.meaning: An adder; read here as a doubled שפי, both legs lame

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Balaam was lame in one of his legs,
as it says: "And he went limping."
Samson was lame in both his legs,
as it says: "An adder on the path
that bites the horse's heels."
phrases.notes: בראשית 49:17, said about שבט דן, which שמשון came from. שפיפון sounds like שפי twice, so both legs.

phrases.english: Balaam was blind in one of his eyes,
as it says: "Whose eye is open."
phrases.notes: במדבר 24:3. It says "the eye," only one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to בלעם with a new teaching about his physical defects, based on the wording of פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the wording of the פסוקים, בלעם limped on one leg and was blind in one eye, and שמשון limped on both legs.

steps.title: בלעם used his body for sorcery
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says בלעם did his sorcery in an immoral way, using his body. It learns this by matching the word נֹפֵל in בלעם's פסוק to the same word in a פסוק about המן.
steps.simpleTranslation: בלעם was a sorcerer who used his private organ. Here it says 'fallen, with open eyes,' and there it says 'and המן was fallen on the couch.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another ugly detail about בלעם and gives a proof from two פסוקים that share the same word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בלעם describes himself as נֹפֵל, 'fallen.' The same word is used for המן falling onto אסתר's couch, where it has an immoral meaning. So the גמרא reads that meaning into בלעם's פסוק too.

keyTerms.meaning: A sorcerer, someone who does magic to predict or control things
Here a polite word for the male private organ
'It is written here... and it is written there.' This is the standard way the גמרא matches two פסוקים through a shared word
Falling or fallen, the shared word that links the two פסוקים

phrases.english: He was a sorcerer by means of his private organ.
phrases.notes: 'He' is בלעם. The word אמה is a modest way of referring to the male organ.

phrases.english: It is written here: 'Fallen, yet with open eyes,'

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב הָתָם: ״וְהָמָן נֹפֵל עַל הַמִּטָּה וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: and it is written there: 'And המן was fallen upon the couch, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of בלעם's flaws drawn from his פסוקים. Step 33 covered his body, and this step covers his behavior.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בלעם performed sorcery in an immoral way, using his body. This is derived from the word נֹפֵל, which also appears about המן.

steps.title: Two opinions about what בלעם did
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a dispute. מר זוטרא says בלעם used his body for sorcery, and מר בריה דרבינא says he sinned with his donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: מר זוטרא says he was a sorcerer using his private organ. מר בריה דרבינא says he sinned with his donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the statement it just made is really one side of a dispute between two אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא agrees with the reading we just saw. מר בריה דרבינא understands the hint differently: בלעם sinned with his own donkey. The next step will show the source for each opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: His female donkey, the same donkey that spoke to בלעם
Literally 'came upon.' A modest way of saying he had relations with

phrases.english: It was stated:

phrases.aramaic: מָר זוּטְרָא אָמַר: קוֹסֵם בְּאַמָּתוֹ הָיָה.
phrases.english: Mar Zutra said: He was a sorcerer by means of his private organ.

phrases.aramaic: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא אָמַר: שֶׁבָּא עַל אֲתוֹנוֹ.
phrases.english: Mar, son of Ravina, said: That he had relations with his donkey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reframes step 34 as only one side of a dispute and adds a second opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מר זוטרא says בלעם did sorcery using his body. מר בריה דרבינא says בלעם sinned with his donkey.

steps.title: The source for each opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains where each opinion comes from. מר זוטרא relies on the נֹפֵל proof we already saw. מר בריה דרבינא matches the words כָּרַע שָׁכַב in בלעם's פסוק to a פסוק that also uses those words.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says he was a sorcerer using his organ learns it as we said. The one who says he sinned with his donkey learns it this way: here it says 'he crouched, he lay down,' and there it says 'between her legs...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the פסוק behind each side of the dispute. The second proof is still being quoted and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For מר זוטרא, nothing new is needed, because the proof from המן (step 34) already supports him. For מר בריה דרבינא, the גמרא uses a different word match: כָּרַע שָׁכַב in בלעם's blessing is matched to the same words in a פסוק that begins 'between her legs.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'The one who says.' Used to introduce the reasoning of one side in a dispute
'As we said.' This points back to a proof the גמרא already gave
'He crouched, he lay down.' These are the shared words for the second proof

phrases.english: The one who says he was a sorcerer by means of his private organ –
learns it as we said,
phrases.notes: This points back to step 34, the proof matching נֹפֵל to the פסוק about המן.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר בָּא עַל אֲתוֹנוֹ הָיָה –
phrases.english: and the one who says he had relations with his donkey –
it is written here: 'He crouched, he lay down,'
and it is written there: 'Between her legs
phrases.notes: שופטים 5:27. The quote is cut off here and continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר קוֹסֵם בְּאַמָּתוֹ הָיָה כְּדַאֲמַרַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the proof behind each side of the dispute in step 35.
steps.raayaObject: The two opinions about what בלעם did.
steps.raayaSupportSource: For מר זוטרא, the word נֹפֵל in במדבר 24:4 matched to אסתר 7:8. For מר בריה דרבינא, the words כרע שכב in במדבר 24:9 matched to שופטים 5:27.
